content.title: About
content.content: Crepe with meat is a thin batter made from flour, eggs, milk and a small amount of butter, rolled around a thin layer of boiled or fried meat. The crepe has a delicate texture while the meat filling adds a rich flavor and extra nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crepes are prepared in many world cuisines: French crêpes, Russian blini, Italian frittatas.
In Russia, meat‑filled crepes are often served with sour cream or tomato sauce.
The thin batter cooks quickly, usually 1–2 minutes per side.
Meat fillings can be beef, pork, chicken or turkey, depending on regional preferences.
Crepes are a popular dish for celebrations, such as Maslenitsa.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The meat filling provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat supplies vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from the meat helps form hemoglobin and prevents anemia.

items.title: Balanced carbohydrates
items.content: Whole‑grain flour in the batter offers slow‑release energy.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and complex carbs helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Using a lot of butter or fatty meat can make the dish calorie‑dense.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat flour contains gluten, which may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Meat must be fully cooked to avoid salmonella or campylobacter contamination.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt in the batter or filling can be a concern for those with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the crepe hot, folded into a pocket or rolled. Top with sour cream, tomato sauce, fresh herbs or grated cheese. It pairs well with a side salad or mashed potatoes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked crepes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in a skillet or microwave. Frozen crepes keep their quality for up to 1 month.
